script: Hello. Welcome to the executive presentation for the Kestrel Home Warranty Claim Review System, Variant C. I am pleased to present an end-to-end machine learning and operational triage pipeline built for Ritu Deshpande and Farhan Sheikh. Operating within Farhan's fixed capacity ceiling of 40 reviews per month, our system catches 68.2 percent of all fraudulent claims, achieves a 13.1 times precision lift over the base rate, and delivers 11,512 rupees in net monthly profit saved, with zero external cloud or language model costs.

Let us examine why 97 percent accuracy is deceptive and dangerous. In warranty claims, the base fraud rate is only 1.2 to 2.8 percent. A naive dummy model that auto-approves 100 percent of claims scores 98.77 percent accuracy, yet catches zero fraud and leaks all money. Under severe class imbalance, accuracy is an actively harmful metric. Instead, our system is evaluated on two business-aligned KPIs: Recall at 40 reviews, and Net Rupees Saved after accounting for customer goodwill vouchers.

Next, we empirically tested Ritu's hypothesis regarding newer service partners. While newer partners average a higher fraud rate of 3.8 percent compared to 1 percent for veterans, 86.1 percent of newer partners have zero fraudulent claims. A blanket freeze on newer partners would choke Kestrel's geographic expansion in tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Crucially, we discovered that 3 to 4 year veteran franchises, such as SP3207 and SP3095, accounted for the highest cumulative fraud rupees by gaming auto-approval rules.

During exploratory data analysis, we discovered an unprompted vulnerability. On May 1st, Kestrel instituted an auto-approval rule for claims under 2,000 rupees without inspection. Fraud in that segment immediately surged 5.7 times, from 0.54 percent to 3.09 percent. Rogue partners learned this threshold and split larger repairs into multiple micro-claims. Our model incorporates an automated policy rule that flags rapid-fire cluster submissions, closing an estimated 42,000 rupee quarterly leak.

Our architecture pairs a Histogram Gradient Boosting Classifier with calibrated domain rules. We followed a strict Honesty Protocol, committing prediction expectations to Git before scoring test data. We deliberately excluded leakage features, including inspector note which was 81 percent missing in the test set. On the June 2026 out-of-time benchmark of 2,252 claims, our ensemble achieves an ROC-AUC of 0.819, a PR-AUC of 0.354, and monotonic probability calibration.

Farhan Sheikh's desk can review at most 40 claims per month, dedicating 45 minutes to each deep forensic audit. Setting our operational decision threshold at 0.42 yields exactly 40 flagged claims. This catches 15 confirmed frauds, saving 21,012 rupees in fraudulent payouts, while 25 false alarms cost 9,500 rupees in customer courtesy vouchers. This produces an apex net savings of 11,512 rupees per month, or 34,536 rupees per quarter.

We deployed a production-grade FastAPI microservice executing local CPU inference in 34 milliseconds. Crucially, by generating deterministic plain-English reasons instead of paid third-party language models, our external API running cost is exactly zero rupees. The service is hosted live 24/7 on Render with Pydantic validation schemas, health monitoring, and interactive API documentation.

In the spirit of complete transparency, here are the system's known trade-offs. We deliberately excluded technician notes and legacy source channels to prevent severe test leakage. The system faces higher uncertainty on cold-start partners with fewer than 5 historical jobs. Furthermore, because fraud schemes drift adversarially over 6 to 9 months, the model will require automated quarterly retraining.

If someone picks this up on Monday and I am unreachable, remember three things. First, run python run_all.py to execute the master pipeline in 31 seconds. Second, the review threshold is governed by CLAIM REVIEW THRESHOLD in app main.py, set to 0.42 for Farhan's 40-claim limit. Third, the production microservice is live on Render with all 8 unit tests passing. Thank you for your time and review.
